findings: All ten 1920 × 1080 PNGs were actually viewed at their original exposure and color; no additional rendering was performed.
At 0 s the complete ringed planet is near center, with teal to the left, purple to the right, blue line constellations and varied white stars.
At 20 s the planet has moved right; at 40 s it is partially beyond the upper-right edge. The colored bands and constellation positions have changed.
At 60, 80, 100 and 120 s the planet is outside the selected view while the aurora and galactic bands remain clearly visible across the dome.
At 140 s the planet reenters from the upper left, partly outside the image and behind the fixed title card; at 160 s it is fully visible left of center.
At 179.9 s the planet, teal/purple bands, seat arrangement and center aisle closely resemble the opening composition.
No narrow bright polar wedges, projection-shell light leaks, blank show frames or unexpected foreground geometry occlusions are visible in these samples.
The title A sky made of light, the original-dome-show subtitle, and the bottom OpenStreetMap attribution are readable and fit their panels in all ten samples.
The dark seat blocks frame a clear central aisle, and the advancing lower progress line remains within the footer.
limits: Only the ten specified frames were visually inspected. This is not a frame-by-frame viewing of the complete movie and does not prove absence of every transient flicker or motion artifact.
The independent media report records full decode of 4,320 frames and 24 FPS cadence; those structural checks are distinct from this sampled visual review.
Some fine grain remains on low-light seating, and peripheral stars are softly elliptical in the wide dome view.
The moving planet is intentionally outside the camera field during part of the program and partially occluded by the fixed caption at 140 s.
The 179.9 s frame supports a near return to the opening composition, not exact byte equality of loop endpoints.
The show is an original artistic composition, not an astronomy ephemeris or a reproduction of an Adler commercial show.
